errors.text: The hypothesis targets stacking-fault energy and ductility rather than coercivity and the orbital-moment contribution to coercivity.
It substitutes the single-phase paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy for the dual-phase FeCoNiTi fcc/C14 Laves alloy.
It omits the central intervention and comparison: rapid-quench stabilization of dual phases and synthesis of the Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 C14-dominant variant.
It replaces the target mechanism of orbital-moment-assisted domain-wall pinning, spin canting, and inter-sublattice antiferromagnetic coupling with longitudinal spin fluctuations.

It does not identify the key state-of-the-art limitation that single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-derived alloys generally have coercivity at or below approximately 100 Oe because the orbital contribution is small.
It misses the reported outcome of approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K and the phase-resolved magnetic transitions at 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
